guidelines.detail: refines XML-06 (The validator rejects the diagram element at line 65 because it is in the model namespace, where the schema expects the DI BPMNDiagram or a relationship as the child of definitions. XML-06 asks for schema-conformant XML in general but does not name the diagram element or its namespace, and LRN-113 covers only the BPMNPlane child, not the namespace. The guideline therefore adds the specific namespa)

new guideline (The generated model used a timer boundary event on the wait to trigger the side action, which then ended the process. The reference uses an exclusive gateway after the wait to test the threshold, runs the side action on one branch, and rejoins the main flow at the stock check. The records M1, F1, F2, F5, F6 show the missing gateway and flows, and G4, G5, X2, X3 show the extra boundary event, flow )

refines FID-03 (The reference names its start event after the title 'Storage management', while the generated model uses the generic label 'Process started' (X1). The description gives a title and no explicit trigger (S1), so the title is the only faithful term available for the start event.)

same as LRN-131 (The reference starts with a start event named after the description's title (M1, S1), while the generated model uses a generic 'Process started' start event that has no counterpart (X1). The description states no triggering occurrence, so the start event should take the title's term. LRN-131 already prescribes exactly this, so the guideline is essentially the learned one, restated in general terms)

The description (S9) says the process starts again with checking whether the order is in stock, which is the check already made at the earlier gateway (S2). rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description asks for a complete BPMN model that includes a diagram layout, so the output must carry shapes and edges for the process: Write the diagram section as a bpmndi:BPMNDiagram element in the BPMN DI namespace (http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI) and place it as a direct child of the definitions root, after the process and collaboration elements. Never write the diagram element in the BPMN model namespace (http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL), because the BPMN20.xsd schema accepts only a DI BPMNDiagram or a model relationship as children of definitions.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description asks for a complete BPMN model that includes a diagram layout, so the output must carry shapes and edges for the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after waiting for an external delivery or reply, a side action (such as a charge or a demand to the other party) is performed automatically if the wait exceeded a stated duration, and the main flow then continues to a later step whether or not the side action was needed: Model the wait as a receive task or intermediate catch event. Follow it with an exclusive gateway that tests whether the stated duration was exceeded. The 'exceeded' branch goes to a task that performs the side action, and that task's outgoing flow leads into an exclusive gateway that merges back into the main flow at the next step. The other branch goes directly to that same merge gateway. Do not model the threshold as a timer boundary event on the waiting activity, do not end the process after the side action, and do not add a separate end event for it unless the description says the process ends there.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description has a title naming the process and states no explicit occurrence that starts the process: Label the start event with the title's own term for the process, not a generic label such as 'Process started'. Do not add a trigger the description does not state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description has a title naming the process and states no explicit occurrence that starts the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that when a condition is not met, the process selects another item and then starts again with the same check that was already performed earlier in the process: Do not add a second decision gateway that asks the same condition again. Model the selection or preparation step that the description names as an explicit task, place it on the branch after the failed outcome, and route a sequence flow from that task back into the existing decision gateway that performed the check. Keep the original gateway as the only place where that condition is decided.
